I farm the way I have learned to farm in Quzhou after 40 years: I keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because it is the most dependable use of my 9 mu, and I leave a smaller part for cotton because I still know how to manage it well and it helps me spread risk. With only two people in the household, I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy, but I will still use better seed and stable fertilizer rates because I am educated enough to trust the numbers and I do not want to gamble with yield. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on it at the key stages instead of waiting on rainfall. On the wheat-maize land, I will push wheat first with solid base fertilizer and timely irrigations, then follow quickly with hybrid maize after wheat harvest so I do not lose the season. On the cotton area, I will keep inputs moderate but not low, especially potassium and plant protection, because cotton punishes weak field management. I will use rotary tillage where it saves time and keeps the field workable, and I will aim for steady yields rather than chasing extreme output.
